title: The Ghost of the Canon
text:
Classic literature occupies an uneasy position in the modern imagination, revered as a repository of enduring wisdom yet frequently read as a museum of prejudices. Critics attentive to the canon have repeatedly observed that the novels considered indispensable were often shaped by the assumptions of their authors' class and era. A reader who approaches a Victorian novel without acknowledging these pressures risks mistaking social convention for universal truth.

Yet to dismiss the canon wholesale is to overlook the subtlety with which such texts frequently undermine their own certainties. Narrators who appear reliable often betray their limitations, and characters whose moral vision seems fixed are sometimes revealed to be deeply uncertain. The enduring value of these works may therefore lie less in the answers they provide than in the scrutiny they invite.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do critics observe about the novels considered indispensable?
options: They were often shaped by the assumptions of their authors' class and era
They were written primarily for children
They were rejected by critics upon publication
They were translated into fewer languages than modern novels

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what is said about narrators who appear reliable?
options: They always provide the most accurate account of events
They are usually the least important figures in the story
They frequently betray their own limitations
They are rarely mentioned by critics

questions.text: What can be inferred about a reader who considers classic novels only as sources of universal truth?
options: They may overlook the social pressures that shaped the text
They are likely to be better informed than professional critics
They will find the characters' moral visions uncertain
They have abandoned the canon altogether

questions.text: Which conclusion is best supported by the final sentence of the passage?
options: Classic novels are valuable mainly for the definitive answers they supply
Classic novels remain valuable because they encourage critical examination
Critics should stop reading the canon in order to avoid bias
Narrators in classic novels are always unreliable

paragraph_translations: Класична література посідає непевне місце в сучасній уяві: її шанують як сховище вічної мудрості, але часто читають як музей упереджень. Критики, уважні до канону, неодноразово зауважували, що визнані незамінними романи часто формувалися під впливом припущень їхніх авторів щодо класу й епохи. Читач, який підходить до вікторіанського роману, не враховуючи цих тисків, ризикує сприйняти соціальну конвенцію за універсальну істину.

Однак відкидати канон цілком означає не помічати тонкості, з якою такі тексти нерідко підривають власну впевненість. Оповідачі, які здаються надійними, часто виявляють свої обмеження, а персонажі, чия моральна позиція видається незмінною, інколи виявляються глибоко невпевненими. Тому тривала цінність цих творів полягає, можливо, менше у відповідях, які вони дають, ніж у ретельному розгляді, до якого вони закликають.
